title: SSDI initial applications, Apr 2027, delay branch
question: Social Security Administration State Agency Monthly Workload Data, Field I Receipts (All Initial), SSA month 2027-04, not seasonally adjusted, first print, in thousands, conditional on a federal statutory or regulatory delay of the 2025 reconciliation law's Medicaid community-engagement compliance deadline being announced on or before 2027-03-31 and pushing the effective date beyond April 2027
resolutionSource: Social Security Administration State Agency Monthly Workload Data
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first official SSA State Agency Monthly Workload Data CSV print for Date Type MO and Formatted Date 2027-04, summing Field I Receipts (All Initial) across all state-agency and federal-component rows if no national row is provided; convert whole claims to thousands and round to one decimal thousand. Use the first replacement file that adds the 2027-04 period; later replacements or retroactive corrections do not change the resolved value. The resolutionDate is the official within-30-days availability by-date implied by SSA's update rule after the 2027-04 SSA month closes; the operative resolver is the first file replacement that adds 2027-04. The conditional is satisfied only if a federal statutory or regulatory delay of the Medicaid community-engagement compliance deadline is announced by 2027-03-31 and pushes the effective date beyond April 2027.
conditionalOn: A federal statutory or regulatory delay of the 2025 reconciliation law's Medicaid community-engagement compliance deadline is announced on or before 2027-03-31, pushing the effective date beyond April 2027.

drivers: official SSA DDS monthly workload Field I first-print resolver
FY2024 DI claims received above FY2022 and FY2023
April 2027 SSA month normally ends on Friday 2027-04-30 and is treated as a five-week operating month

annual DI workload anchors are a downgraded proxy for exact monthly DDS Field I history
state-agency workload data are replaced as a whole file, so first-print capture matters

reasoning.text: SSA DDS initial disability receipts, April 2027 delay branch

Framing and exact resolver: this forecast targets SSA State Agency Monthly Workload Data monthly Field I, Receipts (All Initial), for SSA month 2027-04. The variant is not seasonally adjusted DDS/state-agency initial claims, not OASDI beneficiary stocks, not SSI Monthly Statistics, and not final revised annual claims workloads.

reasoning.call: Opened SSA State Agency Monthly Workload Data documentation and data dictionary.
reasoning.result: Fetched official dataset facts: monthly data start in October 2000; the dataset covers 54 state agencies plus federal components; the expanded file has 71 data elements; Field I is Receipts (All Initial); fields I-M cover All Initial Claims; no summary row is provided; File Version currently has value 2.

reasoning.call: Opened SSA workload time-period and update-policy documentation.
reasoning.result: Fetched timing evidence: SSA counts work in weekly increments as of Friday close; an SSA month may have 4 or 5 weeks and normally ends on the last Friday of the month; the dataset is updated within 30 days of the close of the prior time period; April 2027's last Friday is 2027-04-30, so the within-30-days availability date is 2027-05-30.

reasoning.result: Fetched fiscal year 2024 claims workloads: Disability Insurance claims received total 2,260.6 thousand, worker 2,145.9 thousand, family members and survivors 114.7 thousand; SSI claims received total 1,683.2 thousand, aged 214.1 thousand, blind or disabled 1,469.1 thousand.

reasoning.result: Fetched fiscal year 2023 claims workloads: Disability Insurance claims received total 2,111.9 thousand, worker 2,000.7 thousand, family members and survivors 111.2 thousand; SSI blind or disabled claims received 1,395.6 thousand.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: the best official-source reference class fetched in the draft was recent SSA disability-related claims workload volume. DI total claims received rose from 2,071.7 thousand in FY2022 to 2,111.9 thousand in FY2023 and 2,260.6 thousand in FY2024, equal to simple monthly equivalents of 172.6, 176.0, and 188.4 thousand. The DDS Field I resolver is a monthly flow, so I convert the annual base to a five-week SSA-month analog for April.

Level, momentum, one-off, and policy mechanism: level starts from the FY2024 DI claims monthly equivalent because the official SSA-SA-MOWL.csv is the final resolver but the draft could not stream its tabular rows as exact monthly Field I history. This is a downgraded proxy with a coverage gap: DI annual claims received is not identical to DDS Field I all-initial receipts and excludes some SSI/other DDS intake detail, but it is the public official disability-claims workload anchor available in the draft. Momentum is upward across FY2022-FY2024; April 2027 normally has five Friday workload closes; under this delayed-deadline condition, I remove the near-deadline Medicaid filing-pressure adjustment because the April 2027 deadline would no longer bind.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior = FY2024 DI claims received monthly equivalent 2,260.6/12 = 188.4 thousand; historical sample = fetched FY2022-FY2024 DI monthly equivalents converted to five-week SSA-month analogs using 5/(52/12)=1.1538, giving 199.2, 203.1, and 217.4 thousand; adjustment components = +10.0 thousand for partial continuation of the FY2022-FY2024 upward trend into 2027, +0.0 thousand for the delayed Medicaid community-engagement deadline because April 2027 deadline pressure is absent, and +0.0 for rounding, giving point 217.4 + 10.0 + 0.0 = 227.4 thousand. Interval method uses the values themselves for this flow proxy: sigma = 9.6 thousand across the three five-week analogs, so 1.28*sigma = 12.3 thousand. I widen to a 40.0 thousand half-width, beyond 1.75x, because the fetched annual DI workload anchors are not the exact monthly DDS Field I target, monthly SSA operating flows can vary more than annual averages, and the fallback proxy does not capture April-specific seasonality; final implied bounds are 227.4 +/- 40.0 = 187.4 to 267.4 thousand.

Prior run update: the public prior run for the opposite no-delay condition is used only as a consistency check, not as outcome evidence or a catalog anchor. The delayed-branch point is derived from the same official annual anchors and stated adjustments, with the +6.0 thousand no-delay Medicaid filing-pressure mechanism removed, giving 227.4 thousand.

Counter-considerations: upside risk is that disability-claim filing momentum continues independently of the Medicaid deadline, DDS intake backlogs are cleared into April, or outreach tied to the earlier policy debate still boosts applications; that would land above the interval if receipts exceed 267.4 thousand. Downside risk is that delayed work-requirement timing reduces urgency, applications shift outside April, or non-disability eligibility screens prevent referrals to DDS; the result would land below the interval if receipts are under 187.4 thousand. An outside the interval print would most likely reflect exact monthly DDS Field I seasonality or coverage differences that the annual proxy did not capture.

Review disposition: accepted the critiques to downgrade and label the annual DI workload proxy, clarify the Field I coverage gap, avoid anchoring on the no-delay catalog forecast, use SSA_DATES1.csv for the timing source, and widen the interval for proxy and April-seasonality uncertainty. Rejected rebuilding from exact SSA-SA-MOWL monthly Field I history because those rows were not available in the draft evidence; the fallback remains explicit rather than silently inventing monthly target-series history.

findings.summary: The final resolver is the public SSA-SA-MOWL Field I monthly series, but the forecast rules it out because the run could not stream rows and instead uses annual DI claims received as a proxy.
findings.actionRequested: Use the exact historical SSA-SA-MOWL Field I monthly receipts series, or document a concrete data-access failure and provide a defensible fallback that maps DI/SSI workload totals to Field I receipts.

findings.summary: The stated base rate uses DI annual claims only, while Field I Receipts (All Initial) is a DDS workload measure and may include a different mix than DI claims received alone.
findings.actionRequested: State a base-rate prior from historical Field I April or recent monthly Field I receipts; if retaining the proxy, explain the coverage gap and why SSI/other DDS receipts are not included in the level.

findings.summary: The interval is based on three annual DI proxy values plus judgmental widening, not realized monthly Field I volatility or a clearly calibrated forecast-error distribution.
findings.actionRequested: Calibrate the 80% interval using realized month-to-month, April-specific, or forecast-horizon residual volatility from the SSA-SA-MOWL Field I history; keep any extra policy uncertainty as an explicit additive component.

findings.summary: The +10 thousand trend adjustment to 2027 is only loosely justified from FY2022-FY2024 annual DI growth and not checked against more recent monthly Field I behavior.
findings.actionRequested: Tie the trend update to exact recent Field I observations, or reduce/relabel it as judgmental and explain why annual DI momentum should carry into April 2027 DDS initial receipts.

findings.summary: The reasoning references the opposite no-delay run as a public prior run; this is not outcome leakage, but it risks making the forecast look anchored to another catalog forecast rather than independent evidence.
findings.actionRequested: Keep the comparison only as a consistency check, and make clear the point estimate is derived from source data and stated adjustments, not from the prior catalog/no-delay forecast.

findings.summary: Clarify whether the cited timing file URL should be SSA_DATES1.csv rather than ssa-dates1.htm.
State that 2027-05-30 is a by-date for availability and that the operative resolution is the first file version containing 2027-04, in case SSA posts earlier.
Make the tail cases quantify what combination of trend, month timing, and policy spillover would push the print below 193.4 or above 261.4.
